Advisory fixture provenance
==========================

Ubuntu, Red Hat, AlmaLinux and SUSE records retain their explicit upstream
licenses and original bytes, except documented extraction/projection.
Debian, Arch, Fedora and Rocky advisory fixtures are independently authored
SYNTHETIC schema examples. Copyright 2026 lindm contributors.
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. No synthetic file copies vendor prose or proof.
No network access is required by tests. Schema identity strings do not grant
complete ecosystem coverage or authenticate fictional advisory identifiers.

ubuntu-USN-6859-1.json (3242 bytes)
  GET https://api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/USN-6859-1
  SHA256 e179d515688434574c1835bbff757f0839e37e08fd8d3301168513cbcbdd2f4e
  Vendor https://github.com/canonical/ubuntu-security-notices/blob/main/osv/usn/USN-6859-1.json
  Advisory https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-6859-1
  Copyright Canonical Ltd and contributors. CC-BY-SA-4.0:
  https://github.com/canonical/ubuntu-security-notices/blob/main/LICENSE
  https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode
  Original response includes both jammy and noble; tests require noble only.
  Noble source openssh and explicit binary maps fix 1:9.6p1-3ubuntu13.3.
  No binary-to-source map is invented when that upstream information is absent.

synthetic-debian-DSA-99001-1.json
  Independently authored for lindm; Apache-2.0, Copyright 2026 lindm contributors.
  SHA256 228d3e9c63610162bb21ef042596596274e80a4802714ea4c4184774d83db48c
  Fictional DSA-99001-1 / CVE-2099-99001 and source synthetic-deb-source.
  Debian:12 and the source purl namespace exercise the actual schema identity.
  First fix 3:7.4-2+deb12u3 retains same-upstream Debian revision ordering.
  Controlled predecessor/successor and epoch/tilde versions are not real builds.
  Source-only applicability must not infer a binary package map.
  Schema reference: https://ossf.github.io/osv-schema/
  This replaces the removed Debian DSA original because its data grant was
  unclear. Tracker software licensing does not license the advisory dataset.
  The separately authored tracker cases and coverage map appear in
  debian-tracker-provenance.txt. Live vendor fetch behavior is unchanged.

synthetic-rocky-RLSA-2099-99030.json
  Independently authored for lindm; Apache-2.0, Copyright 2026 lindm contributors.
  SHA256 2ef0fbee82dbd3389348f81299b2db3c8ee42b0ee243146b6df0466286741c3b
  Fictional RLSA-2099:99030 / CVE-2099-99030 and synthetic-rocky-library.
  Rocky Linux:9, rocky-linux RPM namespace, distro qualifier and BaseOS retain
  schema identity. First fix 2:6.2.1-14.el9_4 exercises RPM epoch/revision ordering.
  No binary/source map or complete Rocky package coverage is inferred.
  The original vendor page explicitly attributes Red Hat-derived prose under
  CC-BY-4.0 with modifications, but no explicit grant for all Rocky additions
  or the exact OSV dataset was confirmed. The owner rule unclear=replace applies.
  The original Rocky record was removed; production live fetches are unchanged.
  feed/feed_test.go retains native boundary, digest and RHEL-versus-Rocky scope
  assertions; advisory/advisory_integration_test.go retains persisted matching.

SYNTHETIC Fedora repository metadata
------------------------------------
  All four files below are independently authored for lindm under Apache-2.0.
  Copyright 2026 lindm contributors. They replace the removed original updateinfo
  and repomd fixtures because no explicit grant for those dataset bytes was
  confirmed. Fedora's conditional FPCA content policy is not treated as one.
  Schema reference: http://linux.duke.edu/metadata/repo

synthetic-fedora44-updateinfo.xml
  SHA256 073edc4209285ce5edb8ab70ff0644a7a11c53897326e11680ff8008b5797a16
  Fictional FEDORA-2099-abcdef1234, CVE-2099-99020 and native fixed EVR
  0:8.4.2-12.p3.fc44. The description discloses the CVE; references is empty.
  Fedora 44 / F44, RPM fields and architecture tokens retain schema identity.
  Fictional synthetic-rpm-tool plus seven binary variants exercise package
  multiplicity, prefix filtering and source/foreign-architecture exclusion.
  The source record and i686/x86_64/aarch64/ppc64le/s390x binary records retain
  the original fixture's architecture matrix. Package URLs use example.invalid.
  Additional sudo x86_64/aarch64 identities are intentional: unchanged native
  inventory replay and the console demo require a real installed package name.
  Their advisory ID, CVE, fixed EVR, dates, description and rights are fictional.
  Neither replay nor the demo proves a real sudo vulnerability or Fedora fix.
  A single update remains partial; the demo's authored <updates> container is
  complete only for its fixture-owned controlled repository, not Fedora.

synthetic-fedora43-critical-updateinfo.xml
  SHA256 1e807357b03dde5717b864bbcc71c6ff9cc5a279ca02c9aa20b1c38dc0f55907
  Fictional Critical FEDORA-2099-123456789abc / CVE-2099-99021 and fixed EVR
  0:2.0-1.fc43 for synthetic-critical-library x86_64. Independently authored
  Apache-2.0 supplement, served as demo-authored-critical-fedora-43 alongside
  unchanged real vendor feeds. Its separate Fedora 43 product and two explicitly
  synthetic devices prevent replacement or mixing of vendor snapshots.
  lab/demo/fedora-43-packages.json is independently authored Apache-2.0 inventory:
  SHA256 03f9922aa3b6938a4e8a1a2b9453a7f74162b4e321794f466752f084897b230c
  It contains only the fictional library at 0:1.0-1.fc43. This supplement is not
  a real vulnerability, vendor notice, vendor fix or native remediation proof.
  The original High fixture and maintained native replay contracts are unchanged.

synthetic-fedora45-updateinfo.xml
  SHA256 5aa765c95a1c884f5b54d77635144d7258525cd7b9aa9020bc6e1de8cb42d81e
  Fictional FEDORA-2099-abcdef5678 and synthetic-rpm-loader package variants.
  Fedora 45 / F45 and unspecified nonsecurity type exercise a foreign-release
  record inside a shared container. Fedora 44 findings must exclude it.
  Source, two x86_64 and one aarch64 entries retain the prior schema shapes.

synthetic-fedora44-repomd.xml
  SHA256 b9aa9687f161221357351cd1bd05a329f0a4d75399277b1368383c1065ca5f20
  The updateinfo checksum is the SHA256 of synthetic-fedora44-updateinfo.xml.
  Its relative location names that digest and a synthetic uncompressed payload.
  An unrelated primary entry exercises updateinfo selection from multiple entries.
  The primary checksum is deliberately a fixture value, not a downloadable object.
  Tests separately create compression/transport envelopes and assert raw digest
  pins, checksum corruption refusal, same-origin paths and online/offline parity.
  No vendor signature, acquisition, timestamp or repository completeness is claimed.

Coverage and evidence boundary
-------------------------------
  feed/feed_test.go covers OSV source-only boundaries, updateinfo architectures,
  description-only CVEs, product/module/shape refusals, raw compressed digests,
  repomd checksum/location selection and mixed-product exclusion.
  advisory integration tests retain persisted evaluation, sort/filter/totals,
  pagination, freshness, exceptions, unchanged-byte configuration, offline
  custody, worker leases, publication rollback and persisted finding sets.
  device/advisories_integration_test.go retains unchanged native PackageBatch
  bytes but labels the Fedora assessment synthetic. devlab/console_demo.go
  serves the authored Fedora document and Debian source record.
  Real-feed native evidence lives in lab/ledger.json and docs/verification.md,
  including the Debian/EL/Ubuntu matrix and rolling advisory evidence sections.

Native version vectors
----------------------

dpkg-versions.txt: all 43 original __DATA__ rows, unchanged, from:
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guillemj/dpkg/f4941036b04e787c2803d6359802d6725d2476c6/scripts/t/Dpkg_Version.t
  Original source SHA256 59c8d762acef6cb718dc9b755c04fb070a4ad9e691b57bc0e479e3f188ca36ae
  Extracted rows SHA256 41d0adf1fe8ee5215754547a9f52b279cafbdc06a7be11aa40e573f12f8874e2
  Upstream test file declares GPL-2.0-or-later and no warranty. Only input/result
  data are retained here, not upstream Perl implementation/test machinery.
  https://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html

rpm-versions.txt: all 91 active RPMVERCMP(a, b, result) rows, with only the
  macro wrapper/comma separators changed to whitespace; no vectors invented:
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rpm-software-management/rpm/5dae33c3d0c51c97d5834fe2ecf768b6f5483b81/tests/rpmvercmp.at
  Original source SHA256 55df5ca66658a69b36d251f1ecef151a798baaac47d20a312ac8274718659438
  Extracted rows SHA256 4fd7a79aa7e5b4f9328ab81fccbe9b9da0c0b59b424e58b124fe1d6a140d33a1
  Commented-out known-oddity examples are not active upstream test vectors and
  were not included. Includes all active tilde/caret snapshot cases.
  RPM contributors; repository COPYING provides GPL version 2 for tests:
  https://github.com/rpm-software-management/rpm/blob/5dae33c3d0c51c97d5834fe2ecf768b6f5483b81/COPYING
  https://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html
  Only input/result data retained; implementation independently follows native
  comparison semantics. No native implementation code is copied into lindm.

Adapter boundaries
------------------
  New/Fetch own HTTPS-only TLS-verified retrieval, max four redirects per each
  of at most two documents, two-minute deadline, 128MiB raw document limit
  (2MiB repomd), 512MiB decompression limit, 250000 upstream entries and 500000
  normalized package/range records. OSV individual records are bounded to 2MiB.
  Source SHA256 covers original raw compressed/ZIP bytes, not normalized JSON.
  Optional expected_sha256 is an out-of-band pin; repomd additionally binds its
  companion updateinfo by vendor SHA256. TLS is not a vendor signing-key check.
  Parse is shared online/offline. RPM_REPOMD raw imports contain updateinfo bytes;
  isolated repomd cannot be treated as an advisory document. Offline custody and
  source trust remain with the authenticated importing administrator.
  OSV JSON and single XML update nodes are always partial. A selected ZIP is
  partial. The canonical osv-vulnerabilities.storage.googleapis.com ecosystem
  all.zip URL and full updateinfo can represent complete coverage only within
  configured product/architecture and available source maps. Arbitrary mirrors
  named all.zip do not assert completeness; raw offline imports retain the
  original source configuration and its custody/pin.
  Unknown ranges, module streams, missing source mapping, unknown XML/JSON
  shapes and malformed timestamps fail explicitly; they do not produce clean.
  Rocky OSV cannot establish complete binary coverage. Red Hat/Rocky/Alma are
  not interchangeable. RHEL EUS/module products are not guessed from a major
  version. Unsupported native product formats return errors.
  Fedora adapter derives numeric releases from configuration. Synthetic Fedora44
  fixture coverage is not real-feed proof or qualification of every release.
  Ubuntu LTS mappings are 22.04/jammy, 24.04/noble and 26.04/resolute; noble is
  the only accepted codename alias. Debian supported numeric releases are
  11/12/13; Rocky/Alma vendor major streams 8/9/10. Inventory matching
  remains exact configured release (noble/24.04 alias only), preventing silent
  minor/EUS substitution. Binary architecture aliases do not alter package EVRs.
